The girl realizes that all her parents' tenderness flows back when they are anxious about her illness. She now knows a way to call forth their love and will use this as soon as she has the necessary psychical material to produce a morbid state. Once the child becomes a woman, she marries an inattentive man who unstintingly exploits her work without providing affection or money. Illness then becomes her only weapon to assert herself in life, giving her the rest she craves.

It forces the man to make sacrifices of money and care that he would not have made for a wealthy, healthy woman. If she recovers, he must treat her with care, as a relapse is always possible. Her illness appears objective and involuntary, even confirmed by her doctor, enabling her to use it unconsciously without self-reproach. This mirrors the effective method she found during childhood.

Why does a woman become hysterical later in life? Because it allows her to control people. It draws attention to herself but also makes others obey her whims—essentially gaslighting. The problem is convincing your patient that this is true, so he develops mind control techniques like dream analysis from his book, *The Interpretation of Dreams*. This involves brainwashing the patient by implanting false memories and making suggestions, turning psychology into a form of mind control.

In his dreams, patients can prove knowledge of matters they did not know in waking life. You can make suggestions that the person will believe, effectively controlling their thoughts. Psychology becomes this method today. Floyd gaslights everyone to protect his patrons, allowing him fame and awards. When Nazis come to power, he goes to England where he is well treated and joins the Royal Academy, spreading his views.

His disciple Carl Jung turns these ideas into a systematic understanding of the mind, leading to neuroscience. The problem with this inward-looking approach is that it offers no truth and is merely self-directed, akin to naval gazing. Yet, our society reflects this mindset in popular culture.

Back to Macan, he tells us that true freedom comes from being free together, finding meaning, purpose, and love in each other, not oneself. This leads to the question: did Marxism, liberalism, individualism, Darwinism, or psychology aim to turn us into slaves? You must carry this theory with you and consider its validity.
